heading: Email capture
explainer: Forward, BCC, or set a provider rule to send mail to the inbound address. Mail you send there (from your own address) is always captured for you; mail from other senders reaches you only when they are on your allowlist below. Captured email follows your default scope above.
notConfigured: Not configured yet. The operator sets this when provisioning the instance.
selfAddressNote: your registered address: anything you forward or BCC is captured for you

howTo.heading: How to use it
howTo.forward: Forward an individual message to this address to capture it.
howTo.bcc: BCC this address when you send, to capture your own commitments as you make them.
howTo.autoForward: Auto-forward rule: in your mail provider, forward mail from selected senders here automatically. Provider-side auto-forward (or BCC) preserves the original sender better than a manual forward, so drafted replies address the right person.
howTo.onlyWhatYouForward: Cogeto only ever receives what you forward, never your whole mailbox, and never your password or account access.

allowlist.heading: Allowed senders
allowlist.explainer: External senders whose mail becomes your memory, typically the people you auto-forward from your provider. Other users keep their own lists.
allowlist.empty: No external senders allowed yet. Apart from your own address above, Cogeto is closed by default and accepts no mail for you until you add an address or domain here.
allowlist.spaceTargetTitle: The space this sender's mail lands in

refusals.heading: Recently refused
refusals.explainer: Mail Cogeto turned away, and why. When the sender just isn't known yet, claim them for your own capture in one click.

refusalReason.sender_not_recognized: sender is not a registered user and not on any allowlist
refusalReason.sender_not_allowlisted: sender was not on the allowlist
refusalReason.no_owner: no capture owner was configured (older refusal)
refusalReason.alias_not_recognized: addressed to an alias you have not defined

routingNote: Each rule below names the space its mail lands in. Mail matching no rule lands in {{defaultSpace}}, and mail sent to an alias you have not defined is refused, never guessed into a space.

aliases.heading: Address aliases
aliases.explainer: Give a sender a plus-tagged address such as {{example}} and its mail lands in the alias's space, whoever the sender is. Aliases are yours; other users keep their own.
aliases.addFailed: Couldn't add the alias. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore only.
aliases.refuseNote: Mail sent to an alias you have not defined is refused and shows up under recently refused; nothing is captured for you until the alias exists.
